comb.beats_best_single.spec: curated series where the EQUAL-WEIGHT COMBINATION of the six models has lower pooled mean scaled absolute loss than the best-performing SINGLE model. The combination is built from the point forecasts (mean of y_pred) and then scored on the same series-year scale_abs as the singles -- NOT an average of the singles' losses. Note the comparison is an ORACLE one and favours the singles: 'best single' is chosen with hindsight, while a real forecaster must select in advance

comb.beats_median_single.spec: curated series where the equal-weight combination has lower pooled loss than the MEDIAN single model. This is the decision-relevant comparison, not comb.beats_best_single: the paper's own thesis is that the best single cannot be identified in advance, so a forecaster who must choose blind faces a typical model, not the oracle best one

comb.in_mcs.spec: curated series where the combination survives a Model Confidence Set run that INCLUDES it as a seventh candidate (alpha=0.1). This is a SEPARATE run and does not alter the frozen six-model pool behind mcs.curated_nonidentified

comb.median_kstar_vs_best.spec: median across series of k* for the combination-vs-best-single contest (fewest years to delete to flip whichever of the two wins). Higher = the verdict between combining and selecting is harder to overturn

comb.median_rank_of_7.spec: median across series of the combination's rank among the seven candidates (the six singles plus itself), 1 = better than every single model. A rank consistently near the top without ever needing a selection decision is the practical case for combining

comb.median_winner_stability.spec: median across series of winner_stability for the combination-vs-best-single contest. Read against comb.stability_null_median/p05 (this file's own K=2 exchangeable null, computed at each series' own T then medianed across series), NOT against a bare threshold or a null borrowed from a different panel

cites: S4.4 body: why the rank is what it is
comb.rank6_series.spec: curated series where the combination ranks EXACTLY 6th of 7. The median rank is a summary of a near-degenerate distribution, and this count is what makes that visible

cites: S4.4 body: why the rank is what it is
comb.sn_worst_ratio_min.cross_check: combination_benchmark.csv: min/max of worst_best_ratio where worst_single == 'seasonal_naive'
comb.sn_worst_ratio_min.spec: across the series where seasonal_naive is worst, the smallest (and, as aux_max, the largest) ratio of its pooled loss to the best single model's -- how far the outlier member sits from the rest of the pool

cites: S4.4 body: why the rank is what it is
comb.sn_worst_series.spec: curated series where seasonal_naive is the WORST of the six single models by pooled mean scaled absolute loss -- the pool member an equal-weight mean cannot down-weight

comb.stability_null_median.spec: median across series of the exchangeable-null median for winner_stability under K=2 identically-distributed models, computed AT EACH SERIES' OWN T (per_series_panels' T, not a fixed T~30 approximation), via null_budget.stable_benchmark: 20 independent seeds x 1000 panels/800 bootstrap draws per seed per series (20,000 effective replications) -- what comb.median_winner_stability must be read against, per the discipline established for flagship.stability_null_median (a null computed at different dimensions than the panel it calibrates is a real bug, not a convenience)

comb.stability_null_p05.spec: median across series of the exchangeable-null 5th percentile for winner_stability under K=2 identically-distributed models, same per-series-T computation as comb.stability_null_median; a series' own winner_stability below its own p05 is unusually fragile RELATIVE TO CHANCE at that series' T

cites: S4.4 body: the one cell the median conceals
comb.winning_series.spec: the single series where the equal-weight combination beats the best single model

cites: S4.4 body: the one cell the median conceals
comb.winning_series_null_p05.spec: that same cell's OWN exchangeable-null 5th percentile, at its own K=2 and T, averaged over independent seeds. Its seed-to-seed spread is reported because it is comparable to the gap this threshold is used to adjudicate

cites: S4.4 body: the one cell the median conceals
comb.winning_series_stability.spec: winner_stability of the combination-vs-best-single contest ON the one series the combination wins, averaged over independent bootstrap seeds. Read against comb.winning_series_null_p05 THROUGH comb.winning_series_verdict -- never by comparing the two point estimates directly: this cell's classification is sensitive to seed-averaging discipline (a single seed=0 draw and a multi-seed average can disagree), which is exactly why an averaged, banded estimate with an explicit verdict field is reported here instead of a bare point estimate

cites: S4.4 body: the one cell the median conceals
comb.winning_series_verdict.spec: 'fragile' / 'not_fragile' / 'undetermined' for that cell, decided with BOTH Monte-Carlo intervals in hand. 'undetermined' means the gap between the observed value and its threshold is smaller than the noise in the two estimates -- a real answer, and the one a single-seed point comparison could never return

cites: S4.4 body: five-model combination, seasonal_naive excluded
comb5.beats_best_single.spec: curated series where the FIVE-model equal-weight combination (excludes seasonal_naive, the deliberately mis-specified reference S3.1 documents) has lower pooled mean scaled absolute loss than the best-performing single model, chosen from the same six-single pool comb.beats_best_single uses. Counterpart to comb.beats_best_single, whose six-model version cannot cleanly separate the combination's performance from seasonal_naive's own mis-specification

cites: S4.4 body: five-model combination, seasonal_naive excluded
comb5.beats_median_single.spec: curated series where the five-model combination beats the MEDIAN single model (from the same six-single pool) -- the decision-relevant comparison, matching comb.beats_median_single's convention

cites: S4.4 body: five-model combination, seasonal_naive excluded
comb5.median_rank_of_7.spec: median across series of the five-model combination's rank among the seven candidates (the six singles, including seasonal_naive as an option a forecaster could still pick, plus the combination itself), 1 = better than every single model
